$comment: ENGINE-WIDE defaults for the spec pass. These were literals inside spec-mode-runner.js, changeable only by editing a 9,000-line script. An operator overrides any of them per run with the environment variable named beside each.

toolCalls.$comment: How much an agent may LOOK before it must answer — the most consequential number in the spec pass. Live 2026-08-08 a survey told to open three repositories ran out of calls, reported 'no existing infrastructure, this is greenfield work' about a brownfield estate with 243 matching source files in the first codeline, and a roster was minted on that verdict.
toolCalls.$perCodelineSurveyNote: Multiplied by the number of codelines in scope. A single ceiling cannot serve both an agent looking at one repository and a survey instructed to open every repository in the estate.

perSeam.$comment: Seams that deliberately differ from perAgent. The detective converges by iterating; the PRD change reviewer answers a narrow question.

tools.$comment: The read-only builtin floor granted to every spec-mode agent. Kept here rather than derived as 'every safe builtin' because fetch_url is also safe, and granting network access to the spec pass is a separate decision that must be made deliberately. Plugin tools are NOT listed: they are derived from each codeline's .epam/settings.json, so a codeline provisioned with the codegraph plugin grants codegraph_query automatically.

promptTrim.$comment: How much accumulated coordinator guidance an agent keeps. Live 2026-08-09 a writer's prompt hit 53366 chars against this threshold and was trimmed to the most recent sections — two thirds of its guidance discarded, with a WARNING the only trace. The section count replaced a 1 on 2026-07-11, after a run repeated an identical mistake five retries after being told not to, because a newer heading had pushed the earlier diagnosis out of a single-heading window.

existingFileInjection.$comment: How much of each declared file is injected verbatim into the writer prompt under '## Existing File Contents'. Measured live 2026-08-09 on AMSD-2041: that block was 34,510 of 86,809 prompt chars — 39% — and is paid again on every attempt. It is the term that DOMINATES prompt size: the guidance trim can only cut accumulated coordinator notes, and no amount of trimming touches the injected files. Lowering this shrinks the prompt directly and pushes the writer toward codegraph_query and ReadFile for what it actually needs. Was a literal 400 inside build_implementation_prompt.
existingFileInjection.$note: Truncation stays visible to the writer either way — a file silently cut is how an agent concludes an export does not exist and invents one.

toolPolicy.$comment: What the writer's tools do instead of shelling out. Measured live 2026-08-09 on one story: bash 330 calls / 0.5 MB (56 grep, 45 cat, 21 ls, 16 sed, 10 find) and read_file 202 calls / 1.1 MB, against codegraph_query 1. Three of the four causes were BROKEN TOOLS, fixed the same day: search silently returned '(no matches found)' for patterns that existed (grep fallback lost -E and --include), read_file ignored startLine/endLine and returned whole files, and an unchanged file was re-sent in full on every read. This policy is the fourth part — it stops the shell being used for work the indexes answer better, and only makes sense now the tools it points at actually work.

verbs.grep: codegraph_query (mode "explore" for a feature, "query"/"callers" for a symbol) or the search tool
verbs.cat: read_file (it takes startLine/endLine for a window)
verbs.head: read_file with startLine/endLine

pathOverrides.use: resolve_package_symbol (a symbol's real declared shape) or dependency_contract (which option keys a dependency accepts) — codegraph_query indexes THIS repository only and cannot answer questions about a dependency

bashExplorationRedirect.$note: sed is deliberately NOT redirected: it is used for editing as well as reading, and blocking it would break real work. A verb absent from this map is allowed.

toolPolicy.$readDedupeNote: DISABLED 2026-08-09 after a live failure. The dedupe notice told the model 'call again with force: true'; the writer spent its entire attempt emitting <read_file force="true" /> as TEXT rather than as tool calls and wrote nothing. 13 green tests missed it because every fixture exercised a compliant caller. Re-enable only with a fixture that reproduces a model reacting to the notice.
